Vitamin D: Physiology, clinical applications, dietary sources, and requirements


During puberty, there is a need to increase the efﬁciency of dietary calcium absorption in order to satisfy the rapid growth of the
skeleton. As a result, there is an increase in the metabolism of 25(OH)D to 1,25(OH)2D. Because the blood levels of 1,25(OH)2D
are approximately 1000 times less than 25(OH)D, this increase in metabolism does not appear to increase the requirement of
vitamin D for either boys or girls between the ages of 8 and 18 years. Girls of 9–17 years in Lebanon who took 2000 IU day1
